name: BorderGlow-TS-TW
title: Border Glow
description: A dark, softly shadowed card whose border and a small outer halo brighten with a violet mesh gradient toward whichever edge the pointer approaches, then fade when it leaves.
use: You want a dark card to feel alive on pointer hover without adding heavy motion or an obvious gimmick.
avoid: The glow is pointer-only, so it does nothing on touch or keyboard, and it assumes a dark backdrop.
a11y: The glow responds only to pointer movement and ignores reduced-motion, so touch and keyboard users never see it. (keyboard: n-a, labels: n-a, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A rounded dark card floating on a near-black stage, holding a small outlined 'Pro plan' pill, a bold white heading, a short grey paragraph, a large $24 price and a full-width white button. The card edge is a thin line that can light up violet and blue with a soft halo outside.
behaves: As the pointer moves toward an edge, a cone of gradient light grows along that part of the border and a soft glow blooms outside it; moving away fades both out. In the demo an automatic sweep also runs the light once around the card.
customise: Props set the glow colour, intensity, radius, cone spread, edge sensitivity, border radius, background fill and three mesh colours, plus an automatic sweep. The content is whatever you pass in.
weight: light: One card, a few masked layers, and a short requestAnimationFrame sweep; idle otherwise.
demo: A pricing card reading 'Pro plan', the heading 'Border Glow', the price $24 per month and a 'Get started' button.
issues: The muted body copy is low contrast against the dark card surface.
The effect stacks several CSS mask composites, which some browsers render inconsistently.
polishWhy: Restrained glow and a tidy pricing layout; the dim paragraph copy is the weak point.
